'''Shaukat Hameed Khan''' ([[Urdu]]: '''شوکت حمید خان'''; born 4 September 1941) {{small|[[Pride of Performance|''PP'']], [[Doctor of Philosophy|''PhD'']], [[Fellow of the Pakistan Academy of Sciences|''FPAS'']]}}, is a Pakistani [[Optical physics|optical physicist]] and a [[visiting professor]] of physics at the [[COMSATS University Islamabad|Comsats University]] in [[Islamabad]]. Khan is known for his understanding in [[spark gap]] and [[Plasma physics|plasma]]-induced [[Laser]]s in ionized environment.<ref>{{cite web |title=COMSTECH Award |url=http://comstech.org/cg-award-2017.aspx |website=comstech.org |access-date=8 June 2020 |archive-date=8 June 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200608020744/http://comstech.org/cg-award-2017.aspx |url-status=dead }}</ref>

His career is mostly spent at the [[Pakistan Atomic Energy Commission]] before taking professorship at the [[Ghulam Ishaq Khan Institute of Engineering Sciences and Technology|GIK Institute of Technology and Engineering]] and eventually becoming its [[Rector (academia)|rector]].<ref name="dt150808"/> Besides teaching [[Physics education|educating on physics]], Khan is known for his strong public advocacy for [[Education in Pakistan|scientific education]] in Pakistan and [[sustainable development]] through technology.<ref name="www.pakistantoday.com.pk">{{cite news |title=Leading scientist Dr. Shaukat Hameed joins PTI {{!}} Pakistan Today |url=https://www.pakistantoday.com.pk/2012/04/28/leading-scientist-dr-shaukat-hameed-joins-pti/ |access-date=7 June 2020 |work=www.pakistantoday.com.pk}}</ref><ref name="dt150808">{{cite news|url = http://www.dailytimes.com.pk/print.asp?page=2008\08\15\story_15-8-2008_pg7_37 |archive-url = https://archive.today/20130416142608/http://www.dailytimes.com.pk/print.asp?page=2008%5C08%5C15%5Cstory_15-8-2008_pg7_37 |url-status = dead |archive-date = April 16, 2013 |title = Call to keep national interest supreme |last = Staff Report |date = August 15, 2008 |work = Site Edition |publisher = Daily Times |access-date = 2009-03-12}}</ref><ref>{{Deprecated archive|url=https://archive.today/20120708131500/http://www.akademisains.gov.my/download/istic/2/naim.pdf|title=Strengthening of Technology & Innovation Policy Research Institute at COMSTECH, Secretariat}}by Dr. S. T. K Naim; Launch Meeting of International Science Technology and Innovation Centre for S-S Cooperation.</ref>

==Biography==

Khan was born in [[Lahore]], [[Punjab, British India|Punjab]] in [[British Indian Empire]] on 4 September 1941 and completed his [[Matriculation in Pakistan|matriculation]] in Lahore.<ref name=academy>{{cite web|url=http://www.paspk.org/fellow5.htm|title=Fellows of the Academy|publisher=[[Pakistan Academy of Sciences]]|access-date=2009-03-13|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20070810193641/http://www.paspk.org/fellow5.htm|archive-date=2007-08-10}}</ref> In 1957, Khan enrolled at the [[Gordon College (Pakistan)|Gordon College]] in Lahore where he graduated with [[Bachelor of Science|BSc]] with honors in [[physics]] in 1961, and earned the [[Rhodes Scholarship|Rhodes scholarship]] that allowed him to study in the [[United Kingdom]].<ref name="telecoalert">{{cite web |title=Dr. Shaukat Hameed Khan appointed as CG. of COMSTECH {{!}} Teleco Alert |date=20 July 2014 |url=https://www.telecoalert.com/2014/07/20/dr-shaukat-hameed-khan-appointed-as-cg-of-comstech/ |publisher=telecoalert |access-date=7 June 2020}}</ref>

He attended the [[University of Oxford]] in [[England]], and graduating with [[Bachelor of Arts|BA]] in [[mathematics]] in 1964, and [[Bachelor of Science in Engineering|BSE]] in [[electrical engineering]] in 1965 from the Oxford University.<ref name="telecoalert"/> He started his doctoral studies in physics and became interested in [[optics]] and theory of [[Light]]– the electromagnetic radiation. At Oxford, he played [[cricket]] for [[Brasenose College, Oxford|Brasenose College]], and was noted as a [[Pace bowling|pace bowler]].<ref name="Enterprising Oxford">{{cite web |title=Scholar Talk: Dr. Shaukat Hameed Khan (Pakistan & Brasenose 1962) {{!}} Enterprising Oxford |url=https://eship.ox.ac.uk/old_events/scholar-talk-dr-shaukat-hameed-khan-pakistan-brasenose-1962/ |website=eship.ox.ac.uk |publisher=Enterprising Oxford |access-date=7 June 2020 |archive-date=7 June 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200607011047/https://eship.ox.ac.uk/old_events/scholar-talk-dr-shaukat-hameed-khan-pakistan-brasenose-1962/ |url-status=dead }}</ref> He was also President of the [[Oxford Majlis|Oxford Majlis Asia Society]] in 1962.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Kamal |first=Mustafaen |date=14 March 2019 |title=It was an absolute honour to have Dr. Shaukat Hameed Khan (Majlis President 1962) in Oxford. |website=[[Facebook]] |url=https://www.facebook.com/OxfordMajlis/posts/it-was-an-absolute-honour-to-have-dr-shaukat-hameed-khan-majlis-president-1962-i/1728450167256457/ }}</ref>

His classical work at the Oxford University was based on the [[gas laser]] based on the [[Nitrogen laser|nitrogen]] filled gas tube through the [[spark gap]].{{rp|293}}<ref>{{cite book |title=Scientific and Technical Aerospace Reports |date=1970 |publisher=NASA, Office of Scientific and Technical Information |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=cLxswDPArNQC&q=Shaukat+Hameed+Khan+PhD+Thesis&pg=PA293 |language=en}}</ref> His research work was supported by the funding made possible to study the applications of Lasers by the [[United States]], whose agency, the [[Defense Technical Information Center|DTIC]] eventually released his thesis work as public domain.<ref name="DTIC"/> In 1968, Khan submitted his [[doctoral thesis]], titled: ''The Laser Triggered Spark Gap'', which was approved in 1969, and was conferred with [[Doctor of Philosophy|PhD]] in physics with laser applications in 1969 by the [[University of Oxford]].<ref name="DTIC">{{cite web |last1=Khan |first1=Shaukat Hameed |title=THE LASER TRIGGERED SPARK GAP. |url=https://apps.dtic.mil/sti/citations/AD0693239 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200607011049/https://apps.dtic.mil/sti/citations/AD0693239 |url-status=live |archive-date=June 7, 2020 |publisher=OXFORD UNIV (ENGLAND) DEPT OF ENGINEERING SCIENCE |access-date=7 June 2020 |language=en |date=1 January 1969}}</ref>

== Career in Pakistan government ==
===Pakistan Atomic Energy Commission===
{{Main|Laser rangefinder|Atomic vapor laser isotope separation}}

In 1969, Khan returned to his native country, Pakistan, with [[Doctoral degree|doctorate]] in [[optical physics]] but found research interests in the applications of [[nuclear physics]] when he found employment with the [[Pakistan Atomic Energy Commission]] (PAEC).<ref name="academy" /> Khan was instrumental figure in establishing the [[Laser physics|Laser Group]] in 1969, serving its first founding director until 1981.<ref name="academy" /> In December 1971, he met with [[Munir Ahmad Khan]], a [[Nuclear reactor physics|reactor physicist]], and later attending the conference that was instrumental in decision-making process of developing [[nuclear weapon]]s program in January 1972.<ref name="Pakistan Military Consortium :: www.PakDef.info">{{cite web |title=Dr. Shaukat Hameed Khan. Director Optic Labs PAEC (1985-2001), Founding Head, Laser Group PAEC 1969-1981. |url=http://urbanpk.com/pakdef/nuclear%26missile/memorial_munirahmed.html |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200607230942/http://urbanpk.com/pakdef/nuclear%26missile/memorial_munirahmed.html |url-status=dead |archive-date=June 7, 2020 |website=urbanpk.com |publisher=Pakistan Military Consortium :: www.PakDef.info |access-date=February 8, 2024 }}</ref>

His career mostly spent at the [[Pakistan Institute of Nuclear Science and Technology|Institute of Nuclear Science and Technology]], a national laboratory site, where his earlier work was focused towards designing and building the [[Laser rangefinder]] for the [[Pakistan Army]] in 1970s, building several prototypes for the military.{{rp|6}}<ref>{{cite book |title=Defence Journal |date=1989 |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=qYrfAAAAMAAJ&q=Shaukat%20Hameed%20Khan%20 |access-date=7 June 2020 |language=en}}</ref> After India's [[Smiling Buddha|nuclear test]] in 1974, Khan's interest built in [[Uranium enrichment|weapon-grade enrichment]] of [[Uranium|U<sup>238</sup>]] and was of the view of employing a complex [[Atomic vapor laser isotope separation|laser-based]] [[isotope separation]] as opposed to relatively easier [[Gas centrifuge|gaseous centrifuges]] which was being favored by [[Sultan Bashiruddin Mahmood|Bashiruddin Mehmood]] at that time.{{rp|139–141}}<ref name="Stanford University Press, Brig-Gen. F. Khan, 2012">{{cite book |last1=Khan |first1=Feroz |title=Eating Grass: The Making of the Pakistan's Atomic Bomb |date=2012 |publisher=Stanford University Press |location=Stanford, CA. USA |isbn=978-0-8047-8480-1 |pages=500 |edition=1st |language=en |chapter={{small|(§Mastery of Uranium Enrichment)}}}}</ref> Despite his expertise and advocacy, the program went in favor of employing the [[Gas centrifuge|gaseous centrifuges]] method initially under [[Sultan Bashiruddin Mahmood|Bashiruddin Mehmood]] in 1974 but later went to qualified scientist, Dr. [[Abdul Qadeer Khan]] in 1976.{{rp|141–143}}<ref name="Stanford University Press, Brig-Gen. F. Khan, 2012"/> Nonetheless, Khan continued working on [[Atomic vapor laser isotope separation|laser-based]] [[isotope separation]] with support provided by Munir Ahmad Khan and later used his expertise in laser-based atomic isotope separation of [[Plutonium|Pu<sup>239</sup>]] in successive years– an interest in his research that he remained passioned throughout his career.<ref name="academy" />{{rp|191–200}}<ref name="Stanford University Press, Brig-Gen. F. Khan, 2012"/><ref name="www.paspk.org">{{cite web |title=Pakistan Academy of Science {{!}} Fellow Profile: SH Khan |url=https://www.paspk.org/fellow-profile/?fellowID=70 |website=www.paspk.org |access-date=8 June 2020}}</ref>

In 1981, Khan went to established Optics Laboratory within the Institute of Nuclear Science and Technology in Nilore, of which, he served its first director.<ref name="Pakistan Military Consortium :: www.PakDef.info"/> In 1990, Khan was at a center of controversy when his [[laser rangefinder]] program caught between the rivalry with the [[Khan Research Laboratories]] (KRL) in [[Kahuta]].<ref name="Pakistan Military Consortium :: www.PakDef.info"/> The [[Ministry of Defence (Pakistan)|MoD]] awarded a contract to conduct preliminary studies in laser rangefinders for the [[Pakistani military]] and a prototype was successfully performed alongside British, American, Russian and Chinese [[Laser rangefinder|LRF programs]].<ref name="Pakistan Military Consortium :: www.PakDef.info"/> The federal contract and the funding was later directed to KRL in [[Kahuta]] as a preference, and there was a story published in the ''[[Pakistan Observer]]'' in 1990–91.<ref name="Pakistan Military Consortium :: www.PakDef.info"/> In 1998, Khan became the chief scientist at the PAEC, and participated with his optics team in eye-witnessing the [[List of nuclear weapons tests of Pakistan|nuclear testings]] in [[Balochistan, Pakistan|Balochistan]] in Pakistan.<ref name="academy" />

===Public service and government work===

In 2005, Khan retired from the Pakistan Atomic Energy Commission as chief scientist and joined the [[Planning Commission of Pakistan|Planning Commission]] as a consultant, attaching to the [[Ministry of Industries and Production (Pakistan)|Ministry of Industry]] (MoInd).<ref name="www.paspk.org" /><ref name="n1230608">{{cite news
|url=http://www.thenews.com.pk/daily_detail.asp?id=120079
|title= No more MP-I scale except for Salman Farooqi: Government "All set to fire 22 consultants"
|last=Haider
|first=Mehtab
|date=June 23, 2008
|work=The News International
|access-date=2009-03-12}} {{Dead link|date=October 2010|bot=H3llBot}}</ref><ref>[http://www.thenews.com.pk/daily_detail.asp?id=119448 PC appoints two members on less salary] Friday, June 20, 2008, by Aftab Maken, The News.</ref> Khan provided the strong advocacy for the Vision 2030 program of which he was its director— the Vision 2030 was a policy measure program that aimed towards defining a preferred future for Pakistan from several possible futures.<ref>[http://www.pakistan.gov.pk/ministries/planninganddevelopment-ministry/vision2030/Pak21stcentury/Chapter%2520Wise/Annexures%2520I%2520%26%2520II,%2520107-119.pdf Members of the Vision Themes]{{dead link|date=September 2024|bot=medic}}</ref><ref name="n1230608" />

In 2009, Khan left the planning commission and affiliated with the [[Pakistan Institute of Development Economics]] (PIDC) till 2010 when he accepted an advisory position at the [[Ministry of Industries and Production (Pakistan)|Ministry of Industry]] in 2010.<ref name="www.paspk.org" /> During this time, Khan served on the board of directors of the [[Heavy Mechanical Complex]] and later served as the chairman of the Rhodes Selection Committee.<ref name="www.paspk.org" /> In 2014, he joined the [[COMSTECH]] as its chief coordinator till 2020.<ref name="telecoalert" />

===Academia and public advocacy===
{{Main|Project Topi}}
In 2007, Khan joined the [[Ghulam Ishaq Khan Institute of Engineering Sciences and Technology|Ghulam Ishaq Khan Institute of Engineering and Technology]] and briefly taught courses on physics before becoming its rector in 2008 till 2009.<ref name="academy" /> He later instructed courses on physics at the [[University of Sialkot]] and later became the university's technical adviser on building up the research engineering programs at the university.<ref name="academy" /> In 2014, he joined the faculty of science at the [[COMSATS University Islamabad|Comsats University]] in [[Islamabad]] and was later elevated its chief coordinator.<ref name="telecoalert" /> In 1969, Khan authored a textbook on [[Lasers]], titled: ''The Laser Triggered Spark gap'', which is roughly based on his doctoral thesis, as well authoring a college textbook, "''Optics''" for graduates in physics and engineering in 1998.<ref name="worldcat.org" />

At the public circles, Khan is known for his strong public advocacy for science education, and is a member on a platform of [[Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf]] since 2012.<ref name="www.pakistantoday.com.pk"/>

==Work in CERN==
{{Main|Large Hadron Collider|Compact Muon Solenoid}}

In 1999, the Pakistan Atomic Energy Commission approved Khan's candidacy to join the [[CERN]] in [[Switzerland]] as a senior scientist and a program director for the optics system and Lasers that were installed at the [[Large Hadron Collider]].<ref name="telecoalert" /> At CERN, Khan was the chief designer and had helped design the [[Compact Muon Solenoid]] employed in the [[Large Hadron Collider]] project at CERN in [[Geneva]].<ref>[http://www.eurekamagazine.co.uk/article/15974/Pulsating-detection-work.aspx Pulsating detection work] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20091129130139/http://www.eurekamagazine.co.uk/article/15974/Pulsating-detection-work.aspx |date=2009-11-29 }} by Tom Shelley, Eureka Magazine, 14 November 2008.</ref> Khan serves as the co-chairman of [[Information and communication technologies|Information Communication Technologies]] taskforce.<ref>[http://www.flare.com.pk/news.php?n=362 Sub-committees on IT sector formed ...] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140811105935/http://www.flare.com.pk/news.php?n=362 |date=2014-08-11 }} Flare Magazine, November 29, 2008.</ref> Refer to the [https://cms-docdb.cern.ch/cgi-bin/PublicDocDB/RetrieveFile?docid=3044&filename=bulletin_1999_01.pdf&version=26 CMS Bulletin] from March 1999 (page 13/39)
In 2001, Khan left CERN and re-joined PAEC; he was appointed director of PAEC in 2002. In 2002, Khan headed the [[Plasma physics]] lab at PAEC and printed numerous scientific articles about the discoveries in [[laser physics|laser]] and [[plasma physics]]. He founded the laser programme in Pakistan which has now grown into the Optics Laboratories and a National Institute of Lasers and Optronics with several hundred researchers. He also established the [[plasma physics]] research institutes in Pakistan.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.giki.edu.pk/controlpanel/viewnews.php?id=60 |title=Ghulam Ishaq Khan Institute of Engineering Sciences and Technology |access-date=2009-04-12 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20081023202014/http://www.giki.edu.pk/controlpanel/viewnews.php?id=60 |archive-date=2008-10-23 }}</ref>

==Awards==
===Awards and honors===
* National Talent Scholar, (1959–61)
* Gold Medal from the [[University of the Punjab|Punjab University]] (1961)
* Best All-Round Student, Gordon College (1961)
* An elected [[Rhodes Scholar]], [[Oxford University]] (1962)
* [[Pride of Performance]] (1993)
* Technology Gold Medal from [[Pakistan Academy of Sciences]] (1993)
